import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive analysis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis\n(1000 Cameras Dataset)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_colors = {'Full Frame': '#e74c3c', 'APS-C': '#3498db', 'Micro 4/3': '#2ecc71'}
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, c=sensor_colors.get(sensor, '#95a5a6'), s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_avg_price = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = plt.cm.viridis(range(0, 256, 256//len(brand_avg_price)))
brand_avg_price.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax2, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Brand (Top 10)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# Plot 3: Distribution of Cameras by Body Type and 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#3498db', '#e74c3c'], width=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Count by Body Type & 4K Video', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Megapixels Evolution Over Model Years by Sensor Type
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_mp = df.groupby(['model_year', 'sensor_type'])['megapixels'].mean().unstack()
for sensor in yearly_mp.columns:
    ax4.plot(yearly_mp.index, yearly_mp[sensor], marker='o', markersize=4, 
             label=sensor, linewidth=2, alpha=0.8)
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Average Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Megapixel Evolution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()
plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.92)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
